title: arXiv Physics Daily — 2026-10-28: measurements across quantum, nuclear and particle physics
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart, so this is an inferred notable-paper ranking, not a popularity list; citation evidence is limited for papers only announced yesterday.

sections.title: High significance measurement of reactor coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering on germanium by CONUS+
sections.abstract: The CONUS+ collaboration reports a 10.2σ reactor-antineutrino CEνNS signal from high-purity germanium detectors and a weak-mixing-angle measurement consistent with the Standard Model.
sections.claimed_result: The authors extract 1,555 ± 152 CEνNS events, consistent with 1,701 ± 198 expected, and measure sin²θW = 0.225 ± 0.022 at momentum transfer near 10 MeV.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; CONUS+ high-purity germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, using 1,296 kg·days of reactor-on exposure.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report that the extracted signal uncertainty is predominantly statistical, while energy-scale calibration near threshold is a leading uncertainty in the Standard Model signal prediction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across experiment and phenomenology; the paper gives a quantitative 10.2σ result from 1,296 kg·days and a blind likelihood analysis.

sections.title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of φ, K⁰S, and Λ elliptic flow
sections.abstract: ALICE measures elliptic flow of φ, K⁰S and Λ hadrons in 5.36 TeV oxygen–oxygen collisions, finding mass ordering at low transverse momentum and a 10σ baryon–meson split at intermediate momentum.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say the φ meson follows the K⁰S rather than the mass-similar Λ, supporting quark recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium in light-ion collisions.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; ALICE data from 5.36 TeV OO collisions, with identified-hadron v₂ measured versus transverse momentum in central and semi-central events.
sections.unique_caveat: Flow patterns are indirect evidence for partonic collectivity, not direct observation of a deconfined medium; the interpretation depends on particle-species comparisons and event/centrality analysis.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A large-collaboration result cross-listed in nuclear and high-energy experiment; it combines a first φ-flow measurement in a small collision system with a reported 10σ baryon–meson separation.

sections.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
sections.abstract: A radioactive-ion-beam measurement of ⁵⁴K β decay, compared with ab initio calculations, supports an essential contribution from two-body weak currents in neutron-rich nuclei.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure a dominant transition to a neutron-unbound state at 6.2 MeV, with B(GT) = 0.26 (+0.08/−0.04), and report agreement with calculations that include two-body currents.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental plus theoretical; β-decay spectroscopy at a radioactive-ion-beam facility, interpreted with VS-IMSRG and coupled-cluster calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that VS-IMSRG(2) overpredicts excitation energies; the raw experimental data are not publicly downloadable because they include large files and unpublished isotopes, and are available from the authors on request.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between nuclear experiment and theory; the paper pairs a frontier isotope measurement with state-of-the-art calculations, and its calculated results are available through a linked Zenodo record.

sections.title: Deployed entanglement-based BBM92 quantum key distribution using frequency-converted photons emitted by a quantum dot
sections.abstract: The authors use frequency-converted entangled photons from a quantum dot to distribute a secure BBM92 key over a 1.59 km field-deployed fibre link, sustaining a 206 Hz secure-key rate for 19 hours.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 14.2 Mbit of secure key after 19 hours over deployed fibre, using 780 nm quantum-dot photon pairs with one photon converted to the telecom band.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; droplet-etched GaAs quantum-dot source, quantum frequency conversion, BBM92 protocol and a deployed campus fibre network.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a campus-scale, 1.59 km demonstration over a 19-hour run; the abstract does not establish long-distance or multi-site network performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper reports link length, operating duration and secure-key yield; a closely related earlier setup appears in a 2026 German Physical Society conference programme, an expert-discussion signal but not independent validation of this updated performance.

sections.title: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
sections.abstract: The authors report tunable electron–metal decoherence signatures consistent with quantum Brownian motion, using an electron-microchannel system as an open quantum platform.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say measured decoherence agrees quantitatively with theory and supports electron microchannels as a platform for testing quantum dissipation with free electrons.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; electron motional decoherence in an electron–metal microchannel system.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported system is a specific electron–metal platform; the abstract proposes future tests of Caldeira–Leggett dissipation rather than reporting a precision test of that theory.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-way cross-listing links quantum physics, mesoscopic condensed matter and atomic physics; the authors claim a long-sought experimental realization of a specific decoherence proposal and report continuous tunability.

sections.title: Optically gated transduction enables silicon electrical readout of mid-infrared light
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate room-temperature, zero-bias electrical readout of 6.8 μm mid-infrared illumination by optically gated transduction in a lanthanide-nanoparticle/silicon metasurface device.
sections.claimed_result: Rather than absorbing MIR photons directly in silicon, the device uses MIR-induced changes in lanthanide emission pathways and converts the optical-state change into a Schottky-junction current.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; Nd³⁺-doped lanthanide nanoparticles, an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface and a silicon Schottky junction.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports performance at 6.8 μm; broader wavelength coverage, comparative sensitivity and system-level performance remain unestablished there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete device demonstration reports a wavelength, room-temperature operation, zero-bias readout and 103 μA/W modulation responsivity; the listing is in optics, without cross-listing into another physics archive.

sections.title: Improved constraints on higher-derivative effective field theory extensions of general relativity with GW230627_015337
sections.abstract: A waveform analysis of public LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA events uses a 92-event screening and a Bayesian analysis of GW230627_015337 to constrain three higher-curvature couplings, with results consistent with general relativity.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find all three couplings consistent with zero at 90% credibility and derive one-sided 90% upper limits of 17.1, 11.1 and 18.3 km on characteristic length scales.
sections.evidence_type: Observational analysis; 92 binary-black-hole events from public LVK catalogs, using a modified SEOBNRv5HM_ROM waveform and a Bayesian analysis of GW230627_015337.
sections.unique_caveat: Constraints favor GR under the adopted priors, and the authors caution that comparison with earlier bounds depends on model and analysis assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The analysis reuses a public multi-event gravitational-wave catalog and conducts a full Bayesian follow-up of the event providing the tightest Fisher forecast; it reports quantitative upper bounds rather than a detection of deviations.

sections.title: Search for Neutrino-Produced Long-Lived Particles Using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope
sections.abstract: A search using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope data finds no significant excess of displaced electron–positron decays and sets 90% confidence-level limits on neutrino-produced long-lived particles.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe no significant excess and set 90% CL upper limits on an effective production cross section at around 10⁻³⁸ cm² for laboratory decay lengths of 0.3–100 m.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 2017–2018 SBND CRT Beam Telescope data from Fermilab's Booster Neutrino Beam.
sections.unique_caveat: The search targets LLP decays to e⁺e⁻ and its limits are tied to that signature and the analysed standalone CRT dataset; it is not a general exclusion of LLP models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A large-collaboration search reuses a substantial commissioning-era beam-telescope dataset (2.95 × 10²⁰ protons on target) and reports quantitative limits over metre-scale decay lengths.
